$comment: Scripts of the memory strip, drawn by MemoryStrip.astro. A region's cells are a string, eight cells to a line: '.' free, 'o' other data, 's' the secret (shown as a byte of `key`), 'x' a stale copy of the secret (hatched), '0' zeroed, '?' not written yet. `count` is the number of places the key can be read. `scope` names the region the brace holds while the secret is in use. `refs` cite a leak card (L1 to L9) or a ledger row (R1 to R8). Captions take `code` and [links](/x/).

life-of-a-key.title: The life of a key
life-of-a-key.summary: The same 32-byte key, drawn as eight cells, held in an ordinary array and in a buffer from `Rent` with `isSensitive: true`, step by step.

tracks.label: A buffer from `Rent`
tracks.code: Rent(32, isSensitive: true, out Span<byte> key)

ordinary.caption: `new byte[32]` places an array between other objects on the heap. It starts as zeros.

sensitive.caption: `Rent` hands back a buffer on the pinned heap. What it holds is not known yet: write before you read.

ordinary.caption: The key is written into the array.

sensitive.caption: The key is written into the start of the buffer. The rest of the buffer is still unwritten.

ordinary.caption: The collector copies the array to a new address. The old cells keep the key until something is written over them.

sensitive.caption: Other objects move. The pinned buffer does not, so the key is still in one place.

ordinary.caption: `ToArray()`, or a `string` of the key, makes one more place that holds it.

sensitive.caption: The same copy here would be ordinary memory again: the library cannot reach it. This code makes none.

ordinary.caption: The method returns. Nothing clears the array, its old cells or the copy.

sensitive.caption: `Dispose` overwrites the whole buffer with zeros, the part after the key included, on every way out of the `using` block.

ordinary.caption: Until other data is written over them, a crash dump or a page file can hold all three.

sensitive.caption: The pool can rent the buffer to the next caller, who gets zeros, not your key.

grow-or-append.title: Grow or append
grow-or-append.summary: A key document, a secret as a whole, written into a writer that grows by copying into a larger array, and into one that adds pinned segments. Each cell is a part of the document.

growing.caption: The writer starts with a small array, and the first part of the document fills it.

segments.caption: The writer rents a page on the pinned heap and writes the first part into it.

growing.caption: With no room left, it allocates an array twice the size, copies what it has, and drops the old array with the first part still in it.

segments.caption: The page still has room, so the writer keeps writing into it. Nothing moves.

frames.title: It runs out of room again

growing.caption: Each time it grows, one more copy of what was written so far is left behind.

segments.caption: The page is full, so the writer adds a second segment. Nothing already written is copied or dropped.

cells.heap: ooxxxxoo xxxxxxxx ssssssss ssssssss ssssssss ssssssss

growing.caption: `ToArray()` copies the whole document into one more array.

segments.caption: With two segments, `ConsumeAsContiguousSpan` copies the document into one sensitive buffer and disposes the writer, which zeroes its segments. With one segment it copies nothing.

cells.heap: ooxxxxoo xxxxxxxx ssssssss ssssssss ssssssss ssssssss

growing.caption: The method returns. Nothing clears any of the four.

segments.caption: Disposing the owner overwrites the copy with zeros.

string-or-buffer.title: A string or a buffer
string-or-buffer.summary: A client secret in a request body, deserialized into a `string`, and copied into a buffer from `Rent` with `isSensitive: true`. Each cell is a part of the secret.

string.caption: The body holds the secret, as UTF-8 bytes among the rest of the JSON.

buffer.caption: The same body. It is your code's input, and it holds the secret too.

string.caption: Deserializing makes a `string` of the secret, which the request object keeps reachable.

buffer.caption: `CopyString` writes the secret's bytes into a buffer on the pinned heap. No string is made.

string.caption: `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes` copies it again, into an ordinary array.

buffer.caption: The hash is computed from the buffer, where the secret already is. Nothing is copied.

string.caption: Nothing can overwrite the string, and nothing clears the array.

buffer.caption: `Dispose` overwrites the buffer with zeros. The body still holds the secret until its own owner clears it.
